patterns_data.pattern_details: Florida shows a very large increase in post-acute facility spend for LTSS members, centered in free-standing SNFs and reinforced by smaller NF growth. The increase is primarily driven by more admissions rather than reimbursement alone. Neurologic degeneration and aftercare episodes are the main clinical contributors, pointing to heavier use of facility-based recovery and long-stay care.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the single largest operational cost pattern and it points to a major post-acute utilization lever in FL Medicaid LTSS.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have UM and post-acute teams perform referral, admission, and length-of-stay review for FL LTSS SNF/NF stays, starting with neurologic and aftercare pathways.
evidence_summary: FL LTSS Dual Eligible SNF - FREE STANDING added +$136.1M, driven by about 13,000 more admissions.
FL LTSS Non Dual SNF - FREE STANDING added +$17.7M with about 1,880 more admissions.
Growth centered in neurologic and aftercare stays, including Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC and Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC.
FL NF orthopedic aftercare added +$1.5M, reinforcing the same post-acute care pathway.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorization and facility mapping shifts must be validated before action
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: PA/auth code distribution and Not Mapped facility classifications in FL, IA, NY, and TN
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of apparent spend change is tied to how PA/auth codes and facility types are assigned, especially AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION in FL and NY / TN and Not Mapped facility buckets in IA. These shifts can move dollars between categories without representing a clean operational change. Validate coding and mapping first, then decide whether any remaining increase needs UM, reimbursement, or provider action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Acting on these dollars before reconciliation risks chasing data movement instead of true cost drivers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION logic and Not Mapped facility assignments in FL, IA, NY, and TN, then rerun the affected populations before launching operational interventions.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The groups carry explicit auth or mapping shift and unmapped value signals, so the spend movement may reflect classification changes rather than true utilization or price changes.
evidence_summary: FL AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION contributed +$127.5M, including a +$116.4M state-level validation signal.
IA LTSS Dual Eligible claims in Not Mapped facility types added +$15.8M across volume-led and mixed-cost patterns.
NY / TN AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added +$5.5M, centered on delivery-related stays and two Tennessee hospitals.
Several groups carry explicit auth-or-mapping shift or unmapped-value flags, so these results need reconciliation before business action.

patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a large recurring LTSS cost pattern with a clear utilization and care-management lever.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Pair UM and clinical teams to tighten SNF admission criteria, discharge planning, and NF level-of-care management for neurologic members in CA, IN, and KS.
evidence_summary: CA / IN / KS LTSS Dual Eligible SNF - FREE STANDING added +$41.7M, mostly from more admissions.

IN NF neurologic case mix added +$38.0M, led by Alzheimer's disease and post-stroke hemiplegia diagnoses.
KS NF neurologic case mix added +$12.0M, again concentrated in stroke sequelae, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease.

patterns_data.top_pattern: FL acute hospital spend is concentrated in a small set of authorized provider-product pockets
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: FL Medicaid ACUTE HOSPITAL spend for ABD Non Dual, TANF Standard, and CHIP Standard
patterns_data.pattern_details: Florida acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few providers across authorized Medicaid products. ABD Non Dual shows both higher admissions and higher unit cost, while TANF Standard is mostly a volume story. This mix makes provider-level action more useful than broad statewide policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: The dollars are sizable and concentrated enough to support targeted network, reimbursement, and UM action with named providers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run provider-by-product reviews for Tampa General Hospital, AdventHealth Orlando, and Lakeland Regional Medical Center to separate contract, level-of-care, and authorization opportunities.
evidence_summary: FL ABD Non Dual acute hospital spend rose +$21.1M, with about 1,169 more admissions and roughly +$1K paid per admit.
Tampa General Hospital alone added +$3.7M in the same product and facility pocket, with about +$8K paid per admit.
FL TANF Standard acute hospital spend rose +$15.4M on about 2,263 more admissions even as paid per admit fell, pointing to volume growth.
Smaller additional pressure came from FL ABD Non Dual provider pockets (+$677K) and FL CHIP Standard at AdventHealth Orlando (+$263K).

patterns_data.pattern_details: Delivery-related spend is showing up repeatedly across several states, with one separate NICU severity pocket in FL. Most of the pattern is admission-driven, but certain maternal conditions and the FL NICU case add intensity. This needs maternity-specific clinical and UM action rather than being folded into general acute hospital management.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity and newborn actions differ from other inpatient categories and can affect both avoidable admissions and NICU intensity.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and UM teams review maternity risk stratification, NICU routing, and avoidable delivery escalation in the listed states.
evidence_summary: Delivery-related acute hospital utilization in MD / NC / TN added +$1.5M, including +$814K at ASCENSION SAINT THOMAS RUTHERFORD HOSPITAL.
IN OB delivery and well-newborn case mix added +$810K across post-term pregnancy, severe pre-eclampsia, and gestational hypertension.
FL NICU severity at ADVENTHEALTH ORLANDO added +$981K, tied to Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate.
Smaller delivery-related mixed volume and cost pressure also appeared in NY Family Care (+$697K), OH TANF Standard (+$461K), and KS TANF Standard (+$432K).

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: NC TANF Foster Care ACUTE PSYCH and IP BH
patterns_data.pattern_details: North Carolina behavioral health spend is being driven by a small number of very expensive inpatient psychiatric and acute psych cases rather than broad utilization expansion. Because the pattern sits on low counts and high unit cost, the right action is targeted case and claim review. This is a focused emergence pattern, not a statewide BH trend yet.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few cases are generating meaningful dollars, so early case-level intervention can prevent repeat spend without broad program disruption.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-level review of medical necessity, level of care, and reimbursement for the identified NC BH and acute psych cases.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Multiple groups are flagged for low baseline or small-number events, so a few admissions are driving most of the increase.
evidence_summary: NC TANF Foster Care ACUTE PSYCH added +$1.9M from 46 more admissions, with about +$41K paid per admit.
NC IP BH rare cases added +$1.8M, led by PTSD (+$869K), adjustment disorder (+$457K), and reaction to severe stress (+$332K).
Multiple NC BH groups were flagged as low baseline or small-number events, so a few cases account for much of the increase.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Florida has a separate cluster of ultra-high-cost inpatient cases that should be managed individually, not through broad utilization policy. These include CAR-T and ECMO or tracheostomy-level stays with very high paid amounts per admission. The counts are very small, but each case is financially material.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can distort trend lines and create payment risk if they are not validated promptly.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Complete immediate claim-level clinical and payment validation for these catastrophic cases, including provider outreach to confirm documentation and billed services.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is built on only a few admissions with extreme paid amounts per case, so claim-level validation is required before broader conclusions.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: NY, TN, and IN Medicaid acute hospital and SNF pockets
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Beyond the main enterprise patterns, a few smaller pockets show concentrated spend increases. The NY LTSS SNF pocket looks like a modest mixed volume and unit-cost trend, while the NY and IN acute hospital spikes are essentially one-case events. These should be handled with targeted provider and claim review rather than broad program changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These pockets are too small for sweeping policy action but large enough to justify focused review and repeat-event tracking.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-level audit for the one-case acute spikes and a focused utilization and pricing review for the NY SNF pocket.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Two groups are single-admission spikes and the remaining pockets are highly concentrated, so targeted validation is needed before broader action.
